flags.title: OLBG does not publish odds to a logged-out visitor
flags.detail: The event page for Olympiacos v Fenerbahce (https://www.olbg.com/betting-tips/Basketball/European/Euroleague/Olympiacos_vs_Fenerbahce/4?event_id=535925) shows the market list (Money Line, Pointspread, Game Totals), the tip split per selection and the tipster comments, but every 'WIN @' field is empty. The only price-like values on the page come from individual tipsters' comments ('2.50 hcap', '169.50 hcap'), which are one person's taken line, not a market consensus.
flags.action: No OLBG price is quoted anywhere on this site. Where no official number existed, our price is derived from OLBG's published tip share with a Laplace prior, and every such row is labelled 'OLBG tip share' rather than presented as a market price.

flags.title: OLBG's displayed times are not a single timezone
flags.detail: OLBG prints 'Today 20:00' for the MLB World Series game whose official first pitch is 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z, i.e. 20:00 US Eastern on 23 October. European fixtures are printed in UK local time (the URC match centre gives 14:45 local for Cardiff v Sharks, matching OLBG's 14:45). The column is therefore a mix of US Eastern and UK local, not UTC.
flags.action: The displayed string is copied verbatim into every table and is never converted. Where an official start time exists (MLB, NHL) it is stored separately in data/liveboard/inputs.json.

flags.title: No official injury or availability list was obtained for any fixture
flags.detail: The brief asks every high-confidence prediction to carry relevant, verifiable injuries. No official injury report was retrieved in this session for any of the twelve fixtures that carry a written prediction or for any other row: the NHL feed publishes rosters but not injury status, the MLB feed used here was the standings endpoint, and club-level injury pages were not read.
flags.action: No prediction asserts an injury, a suspension or a return. Every prediction carries an explicit 'no official list was obtained' line where an injury sentence would otherwise sit. This is a gap against the brief, disclosed rather than filled with invented team news.

flags.title: Five written predictions per sport was not reached
flags.detail: Seven predictions were written: three on the MLB World Series fixture, two on URC Round 4 fixtures and two on snooker matches. That is three sports out of fifteen. The blockers are named individually in F-01 to F-08; in each case the missing ingredient is an official current-form input, without which a thirty-word prediction would have to invent form, recent results or statistics.
flags.action: The shortfall is published on the Coverage page sport by sport rather than being smoothed over. No prediction was written from a tip share alone.

flags.title: The −250 floor and the 70% floor overlap in a narrow window
flags.detail: A fair 70% probability is about −233 and a fair 75% is about −300 after a five per cent margin. Requiring both 'at least 70%' and '−250 or longer' therefore selects roughly the 70–75% band. Strong selections such as Gloucester at 89% (−543) and Mark Williams at 88% are correctly excluded from the band, and the Top picks page shows them separately so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
flags.action: Both conditions are applied exactly as the brief states. The five qualifying single matches are listed in the executive summary; the per-sport top five ignore the band and show the true highest-confidence rows.

flags.title: OLBG pagination was not followed
flags.detail: Each sport hub ends with a 'Load More Tips' control. Only the first rendered page of each hub was captured, so the 128 fixture rows are a slice of OLBG's card for 23 October, not its complete inventory. The count is stated on the Coverage page instead of being described as a full list.
flags.action: Every table is labelled as a first-page capture. Nothing on the site claims to be OLBG's complete card.

flags.detail: The world list captured eleven players and the one-year list eleven players; Scott Donaldson is on neither, so his strength could not be measured. Jak Jones is fourth on the one-year list at £141,000, which is the only official number behind that fixture's price.

flags.title: No official US Grand Prix session time or grid was captured
flags.detail: The Formula 1 results page supplied the 2026 drivers' standings, which is the only official input used. Neither the official race start time nor a grid or qualifying result was obtained; OLBG's '25 Oct 16:00' is its own display string.
flags.action: Only the race-winner market is priced, from championship points share discounted for single-race variance, and it is labelled low confidence at 7.2%. No motor racing prediction was written.

flags.title: NHL club records were not obtained; the two games are priced off the feed's own moneylines
flags.detail: The NHL schedule endpoint publishes a moneyline per club but not a win-loss record, and the standings endpoint returned thirty-two clubs across eight chunks of which only one was read (Carolina, Edmonton, Boston and Vegas). Montreal, Chicago, Tampa Bay and Colorado records were therefore not captured, so the price is the mean implied probability of the published prices rather than a strength model.
flags.action: Both NHL rows are labelled official-model with the odds basis stated in full. No NHL prediction was written because no form line could be sourced.

flags.title: Only one baseball fixture exists, so the five-per-sport target cannot apply
flags.detail: The MLB schedule for 23 to 30 October 2026 contains six games, all World Series games between Tampa Bay and Milwaukee. OLBG lists the first of them. There is no second baseball fixture to write about, so the three baseball predictions are three different markets on the same game rather than five different matches.
flags.action: All three are separately labelled by market (money line, game totals, run line) and the reader is told they are the same fixture.
